assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cytosine and adenine base editors convert single bases in living cells with no double-strand break, using engineered deaminases (incl. directed evolution of a TadA RNA-deaminase into a DNA adenine deaminase). Original, chemically driven, and already in clinical use; a clear invention with lasting reach across biology and medicine.
assessment.attribution: Liu led the concept and both platforms; Komor (first author of the C-to-T editor) and Gaudelli (A-to-G editor) did the decisive experimental work. A prize for Liu alone or Liu with the two is plausible; Kondo and Nishida's parallel deaminase-fusion work is not supported here as co-equal.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly confirmed independently and now in human trials with first clinical benefit reports; recognition is timely. Overlap with the 2020 CRISPR prize and with prime editing (B026) must be handled so the chemical invention is credited coherently.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as chemistry or physiology/medicine territory after the 2020 CRISPR prize.
Allocation between Liu and the first authors versus the Japanese deaminase-fusion work.
Long-term clinical safety and off-target data are still accumulating.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis opened mild single-electron routes to bond constructions widely used in drug discovery and industrial synthesis. Broad, conceptually clear and transformative for synthetic methodology.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread over many groups (Yoon, Stephenson, MacMillan, Nicewicz, Fukuzumi, König, Melchiorre). I propose Yoon, Stephenson and MacMillan as the 2008-2009 originators, but MacMillan already holds a 2021 prize for organocatalysis, so a fair configuration may weigh others more.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of independent confirmation and industrial uptake; the field is mature. Timing is solid, though the long tail of contributors complicates a clean selection.
uncertainties: MacMillan's earlier prize may weigh against him in this configuration.
Priority questions with earlier Ru/Ir photochemistry (Kellogg, Fukuzumi, Deronzier) and between near-simultaneous reports.
Whether the Nobel scope is the concept or specific later developments (dual catalysis).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation by PROTACs and molecular glues redefines how small molecules act, by hijacking E3 ligases to eliminate proteins. It is a new pharmacological modality with a dozen clinical candidates.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies introduced the PROTAC concept (2001); Ciulli provided the VHL ligands and structural rationale; Handa/Ito (thalidomide-cereblon) and Gray and others complete the molecular-glue story. A three-person prize is defensible but cuts out part of the field.
assessment.maturity: Strong preclinical confirmation and many clinical trials, but no fully approved PROTAC drug, so impact in patients is not yet settled. Possibly slightly premature.
uncertainties: No approved PROTAC drug yet.
Credit split between PROTAC and molecular glue/cereblon discoveries, including Handa and Ito.
Overlap with the 2004 ubiquitin prize context.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers took solar cells from about 4 percent to over 25 percent efficiency within a decade, reshaping photovoltaics research and opening a vast solid-state materials family with exceptional optoelectronic properties.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka made the first perovskite-sensitized cell (2009); Park and Snaith produced the solid-state devices that triggered the field (2012); Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis made major contributions. Credit is contested, so I propose Miyasaka, Park and Snaith.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed everywhere, but operational stability and commercial scale-up remain unresolved. The science is mature, the technology arguably not yet.
uncertainties: Device stability and lead toxicity may keep the technology from proven lasting impact.
Disputed allocation among Miyasaka, Park, Snaith, Grätzel and Seok.
Whether the contribution is chemical discovery or device engineering.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Machine-learned interatomic potentials deliver near-quantum accuracy at force-field cost, enabling simulations of materials and reactions at scales previously inaccessible. A genuine methodological shift across materials and molecular chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Behler and Parrinello (2007 neural-network potential) founded the approach; Bartók and Csányi (Gaussian approximation potentials, SOAP) built the second main branch. Parrinello also appears in B004 and B027, which may complicate overall configuration.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted and increasingly validated, but transferability, uncertainty and long-time robustness are still being tested; arguably early.
uncertainties: Maturity: rapid evolution, with foundation-model potentials changing the landscape.
Overlap in personnel with other computational candidates.
Division between the Behler-Parrinello and Bartók-Csányi lineages.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Surfactant-templated ordered mesoporous silicas (MCM-41, SBA-15, KIT-6) gave tunable pore sizes of 2-50 nm, extending molecular-sieve chemistry beyond zeolites and enabling catalysis, adsorption and nanocasting. From my structural-chemistry perspective the characterization of such nanoporous solids was decisive, and the concept is original and clear.
assessment.attribution: Kresge and Beck (Mobil) discovered MCM-41; Inagaki independently reported FSM-16; Stucky/Zhao developed SBA-15 and related phases; Ryoo pioneered carbon replication. A fair prize of Kresge, Ryoo and Zhao is conceivable but excludes Beck, Inagaki and Stucky.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of confirmation; the impact is broad but the field has partly matured toward MOFs and COFs, and the 2025 prize recognized MOFs. Timeliness is less pressing than for newer candidates.
uncertainties: Disputed priority and distribution among Mobil, Japanese (Inagaki, Kuroda) and Stucky/Zhao work.
Whether the porous-materials area is considered covered by the 2025 MOF prize.
Industrial impact is more limited than that of zeolites.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Palladium-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling (Buchwald-Hartwig amination) is a staple of pharmaceutical synthesis, enabling arylamine construction under practical conditions. Extremely well-established, with ligand design driving scope.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the ligand-controlled catalytic systems; Kosugi and Migita's tin-amide chemistry is a precursor. A two-laureate prize of Buchwald and Hartwig is the natural configuration.
assessment.maturity: Over 25 years of independent confirmation and heavy industrial usage; the work is certainly mature. The 2010 Pd cross-coupling prize reduces novelty of the field, though not of this reaction.
uncertainties: The committee might regard this as extension of the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
Role of Kosugi, Migita and earlier precedent.
Hartwig is also credited in B015, which may split attention.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers allows structure determination from nano- and microcrystals before radiation damage and time-resolved studies of reactions. This is close to my own interest in structures from tiny crystals.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the first demonstrations (2011) with Fromme, Hajdu, Schlichting, Spence and others; Hajdu conceived the diffraction-before-destruction idea. The credit is shared across a large team, making a three-person selection fragile.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed at multiple facilities, with growing numbers of structures, but access is limited and the impact on mainstream structural biology is still modest relative to cryo-EM.
uncertainties: Large, collaborative credit pool; Spence, Schlichting, Barty and others may have equal claim.
Impact relative to cryo-EM and microED is debated.
Technique depends on facility access.
